findings.excerpt: the `@[simp]` form, and `simp` reaches this one through it, so this lemma is not itself `simp`.
findings.problem: The docstring says `simp` reaches the sign-free simple-root equation through the general `@[simp]` lemma `_of_ne`. Reading the sources, I doubt it does. On a simple root, `_of_ne` produces `transvectionUnit (Fin.rev_injective.ne _) ((-1) ^ (↑i.castSucc + ↑i.succ + 1) * c)`. The sign is left as an unevaluated power, and nothing simp-tagged shows it equals 1. That needs `Even.neg_one_pow`, which is a conditional lemma and not simp. The result also has indices `(i.succ).rev` and `(i.castSucc).rev`, while the simple-root lemmas state `i.rev.castSucc` and `i.rev.succ`. `Fin.rev_succ` and `Fin.rev_castSucc` are not simp lemmas in core. The proofs of the two simple-root lemmas have to do these rewrites by hand with `simpa only [Fin.rev_succ, Fin.rev_castSucc, hsign, one_mul]`. So `simp` does not reach the canonical sign-free statement. The more specific, more useful rules are exactly the ones left out of the simp set. The SL file also has to restate and re-prove the simple-root versions.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `typeAGraphAutomorphism_transvectionUnit` and `typeAGraphAutomorphism_transvectionUnit_lower` as `@[simp high]`, so they win over `_of_ne` on `castSucc i ≠ succ i` and `succ i ≠ castSucc i` instances. This is probably better than the alternative of adding a simp lemma that evaluates the sign. Otherwise, correct the docstrings so they do not claim `simp` reaches these forms. The same change would apply to the `transvection` analogues in the SL file.
findings.benefit: Simple-root transvections would normalise to the parameter-preserving form, which is what the Chevalley-carrier code in `StandardCarrier/GraphAutomorphism.lean` uses (it cites the simple-root lemmas explicitly). Users would no longer be left with an unreduced `(-1)^(…)` sign factor and mismatched `rev` indices after `simp`. The docstrings would also match what `simp` actually does.

evidence.excerpt: simpa only [Fin.rev_succ, Fin.rev_castSucc, hsign, one_mul] using
theorem rev_succ (k : Fin n) : rev (succ k) = castSucc (rev k)

findings.problem: This is a simp lemma whose LHS is the fully generic equation `typeAGraphAutomorphism r A g = h` for arbitrary `g h`. Every such equation is rewritten into a statement about three explicit matrix products, with `Q` unfolded as a coerced unit. That is an unwanted expansion. Examples are goals such as `φ g = g`, or equations where `h` is a variable or a group word. There is also no simp lemma for the symmetric orientation `h = φ g`. The transposed variant `…_transpose_mul_conjugator_mul_eq` is deliberately not simp, so the file has two equally valid characterisations, and the simp set picks one arbitrarily. Its only downstream uses are explicit `rw` calls in `UnitaryFixedPoints.lean`. Nothing in the file's uses relies on simp firing it. Because the eliminated form is the group-level equation, simp users lose the ability to use `eq_comm` or the group structure afterwards.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `typeAGraphAutomorphism_eq_iff_mul_conjugator_mul_transpose_eq`. Both invariance-equation characterisations would then be non-simp lemmas, used by explicit `rw`/`simp only` as `UnitaryFixedPoints.lean` already does.
findings.benefit: `simp` would no longer silently turn any equation `φ g = h` into a matrix equation involving `Q`, which can obscure group-level goals and interact badly with the involution and diagonal/transvection simp lemmas. Behaviour would also be symmetric between the two invariance-equation lemmas.
